title: Interior and exterior angles of convex polygons
summary: Calculate polygon angle sums, regular angles and side counts.
objectives: Calculate the interior-angle sum of any convex polygon.
Relate interior and exterior angles of regular polygons.
Determine a polygon's number of sides from angle information.

sections.title: From triangles to any convex polygon

blocks.text: Drawing diagonals from one vertex divides an n-sided convex polygon into n - 2 triangles, so its interior-angle sum is (n - 2)180°. One exterior angle at each vertex always totals 360°.

Drawing diagonals from one vertex divides a convex n-sided polygon into n−2 triangles, so its interior-angle sum is (n−2)×180°. One exterior angle at each vertex, taken in the same direction, always totals 360°. In a regular polygon all exterior angles are equal.

For a regular polygon, exterior angle=360°/n and interior angle=180°−exterior angle. To recover n, divide 360° by the exterior angle. If an interior angle is given, first subtract it from 180°. The resulting side count must be a whole number at least 3.

blocks.text: Do not divide 360° by an interior angle. Convert to the exterior angle first. The formula (n−2)×180° gives the total interior sum, not one interior angle unless you divide by n for a regular polygon.

prompt.text: Find the interior-angle sum of a hexagon.

feedback.text: A hexagon has four triangles, so 4 × 180° = 720°.
